mutant.description: THE CONTROL THAT HAD TO BE ABLE TO FAIL IS S6-AC2's PRE-BURST ALARM STATE, and it is the one the face names first. The criterion grades the ALARM TRANSITIONING, not the rule blocking, and its whole load is carried by the negative control: if the alarm is ALREADY in ALARM when the burst starts, a subsequent ALARM reading is indistinguishable from a standing condition and the criterion certifies nothing. This control was not simulated -- it FIRED TWICE ON REAL STATE and blocked two attempts before it passed.
mutant.expected: If the pre-burst state is anything other than a freshly-measured OK, the run is refused and no transition is claimed.
mutant.observed: FIRED TWICE, BOTH TIMES BLOCKING A CLAIM THIS SEAT WOULD OTHERWISE HAVE MADE. (1) At 23:46:37Z the WAF alarm was already in ALARM pre-burst: a peer lane's probe (UA opal-s7-probe) had blocked 60 requests at 23:44:00Z, two minutes before the alarm existed. A staged burst then would have been uninterpretable. (2) A second attempt read OK at 23:52:26Z, but the OK->ALARM transition at 23:52:36Z fired on the PEER'S 23:51 datapoint (3.0) -- ten seconds after the read and two minutes BEFORE this seat's burst -- so that burst SUSTAINED an already-breaching alarm and the transition is NOT claimed as this seat's. Only the third run, with ZERO gap between the control read and the burst (OK measured 00:02:36Z, burst started 00:02:36Z), produced a transition this seat can own. THE CONTROL ALSO CHANGED THE DESIGN: because the auth path carries live peer and user traffic, timing alone can never attribute a transition here, so attribution was moved to CONTENT -- magnitude and User-Agent -- which no coincidence can forge.

determinism.method: The staged burst was run TWICE with identical shape (240 requests, same fixture-identity form, same User-Agent) at 23:54:15Z and at 00:02:36Z, and the resulting AuthThrottled metric was summed independently on each run.
determinism.observed: Both runs produced the identical status histogram {401: 5, 429: 235} and both produced exactly 235 counted throttle events on the metric plane -- run 1 as a single 235.0 datapoint at 23:54, run 2 split 190.0 at 00:02 + 45.0 at 00:03 = 235 across the two minute-buckets it straddled. Same input, same count, twice; the bucket split differs only because the second run crossed a minute boundary.
